e.meaning: of Mithra; tied to Persian mehr, sun and kindness
e.etymology: From Middle Persian Mihran, the name of one of the great noble houses of ancient Iran. It is related to mehr and to Mithra, the old Iranian deity of light and covenants.
A respelling of Clyde, which comes from the River Clyde that runs through Glasgow.
A short form of Miroslav and other Slavic names built on mir, peace or world. In Catalan it is a separate old name, best known as the surname of painter Joan Miro.
namesakes: Joan Miro (Spanish painter; Miro was his surname)

assoc.t: Miro, online whiteboard app for teams

e.etymology: A respelling of Zariah with X in place of Z. Zariah is itself a modern American name in the family of Zara and Zaria.
The English word, from Greek epos, a word or tale, first applied to long heroic poems such as the Iliad and now also everyday slang for anything impressive.
A respelling of Bowen, a Welsh surname shortened from ab Owain, son of Owen.

e.meaning: from Evreux, a town in Normandy
e.etymology: The American spelling of Devereux, an Anglo-Norman surname for someone from Evreux in Normandy.
namesakes: Blanche Devereaux (Rue McClanahan's character on The Golden Girls)

e.etymology: The ordinary English word, given as a hopeful first name. Winner is also an old English and German surname.
A modern spelling with more than one possible source: it can follow Isla or Ayla, or the Hebrew Elah, a word for the terebinth tree.
A modern American coinage that puts an N in front of Isaiah, the Hebrew prophet's name.
A respelling of Kailani, from Hawaiian kai, sea, and lani, sky or heaven, written here to echo Kayla.
A modern American coinage that adds the -ly ending of Everly and Kimberly to the word River.
A short modern name that reads as Zen written with an X. It also matches the Greek root xen-, stranger or guest, found in Xenia and Xenophon.
An elaboration that reads as Eva joined to Nora. It was the name of the Wicked Witch of the East in the 2013 film Oz the Great and Powerful.
namesakes: Evanora (Rachel Weisz's wicked witch in Oz the Great and Powerful)

e.etymology: A short form of Gillian or Jillian, the medieval English form of Juliana, from the Roman family name Julius. Its long use as an everygirl name shows in the rhyme Jack and Jill.

assoc.t: Jill of the nursery rhyme Jack and Jill

e.etymology: A modern spelling of Alicia, the Latinized form of Alice, which goes back through Old French to the Germanic name Adalheid, noble kind.
An English surname that began as an Anglo-Norman nickname, lou, wolf, with a diminutive ending. Lowell is the same name in another spelling.
The Spanish and Portuguese form of Homer, from Greek Homeros, the name given to the poet of the Iliad and the Odyssey. The Greek word homeros means a hostage or pledge.
e.note: In Latin American Spanish, Homer Simpson is called Homero.

e.etymology: A Spanish and Portuguese variant of Miriam, the Hebrew name of Moses's sister, whose meaning has been debated for centuries. Mirian is separately a man's name borne by early Georgian kings.
An English spelling of Johanna, the feminine of Johannes (John), from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious.
A spelling of Kiana, a name that spread in the US in the 1980s and 1990s and is often explained as a Hawaiian form of Diana.
An American coinage that joins Ray to the -von ending of names like Devon and Javon.
A short form of Alicia or Aleisha, which go back through Alice to the Germanic name Adalheid, noble kind.
From Greek Phaidra, from phaidros, bright. In myth Phaedra is the wife of Theseus, and her story was retold by Euripides, Seneca and Racine.
namesakes: Phaedra Parks (The Real Housewives of Atlanta)
e.note: The myth is a tragedy: Phaedra falls for her stepson and takes her own life.

e.etymology: The French, German and Scandinavian form of Matilda, from Germanic words for might and battle.
A respelling of Gracie, the pet form of Grace, from Latin gratia.
An Arabic-style name that came into American use in the late 1980s through the rapper Rakim of Eric B. & Rakim. It sits close to Karim, Rahim and Hakim.

assoc.t: Rakim, hip-hop MC of Eric B. & Rakim

e.etymology: A respelling of Xavier that writes out the ex-ZAY-vee-er pronunciation. Xavier comes from the Basque place name Etxeberria, new house, the birthplace of Saint Francis Xavier.
The Latin form of Greek Herakles, read as the glory of Hera, the name of the hero famous for his twelve labors.

assoc.t: mythic strongman, hero of Disney's 1997 film

e.note: The name is a byword for great strength, so expect comparisons and jokes.

e.etymology: A spelling of Dallin, a surname turned first name that is especially common in Utah.
The Spanish double name Maria Fernanda written as one word, as US birth records often do. Fernanda is the feminine of Fernando, a Germanic name read as bold journey.
